rounds.text: Cindrella Hotels Ltd trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.61x on a book value of ₹ 31.1 with the share price at ₹ 50.0 [E2], and offers a tangible dividend yield of 1.99% [E4]. The underlying business is experiencing a powerful acceleration in its top line, demonstrating a robust compounded sales growth rate of 34% over 5 years [E15], a multi-year sales uptrend [E64], and a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 13% [E17]. This strong commercial momentum is further supported by recent positive operational signals including year-over-year sales growth of 7% [E61] and quarter-over-quarter sales expansion [E63]. Profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 24% indicates that the company is actively beginning to outperform market expectations [E55]. Conceded: E18, E20, and E21.

Cindrella Hotels Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is entirely detached from its underlying earnings power, sitting at a trailing P/E of 94.7 [E1] or up to 98.66x against a sector benchmark of just 26.16x [E6]. This massive earnings multiple looks exceptionally precarious when measured against the company's weak profitability trends, which include a 3-year compounded profit growth of -26% [E20] and a TTM profit contraction of -5% [E21]. Furthermore, the business generates a return on assets (ROA) of only 1.19%, lagging behind the sector benchmark of 2.18% [E8]. Long-term wealth creation has been virtually nonexistent, evidenced by a 10-year compounded profit growth of -2% [E18] and a modest 10-year share price growth of 9% [E22]. Conceded: compounded sales growth reached 34% over 5 years [E15]. Nevertheless, investors are paying a staggering multiple for a shrinking bottom-line [E21] and subpar asset efficiency [E8].

Conceded: the trailing P/E of 94.7x or 98.66x stands well above the sector benchmark of 26.16x [E1, E6]. However, this headline multiple ignores a business experiencing a powerful top-line acceleration, with multi-year sales uptrends, quarter-over-quarter sales growth, and a 7% year-over-year sales increase [E61, E63, E64]. This top-line momentum is best demonstrated by an impressive 34% compounded sales growth over five years and a 13% expansion over the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. Furthermore, the market capitalisation sits at a modest ₹ 18.0 Cr while the stock trades low in its 52-week range at just 15% of the way up, offering a compelling entry point relative to its asset backing [E3, E5, E7]. The price-to-book ratio is a modest 1.61x to 1.67x, actually trading at a discount to the sector benchmark price-to-book of 2.3x [E2, E7].
